sentences.text:
Permanent injunction restraining the defendants, their Media Houses,
representatives, agents, servants or any persons claiming through or under them either jointly and severally, from broadcasting through its Electronic Media Channel or by any other Print or Electronic Media, any defamatory, derogatory, unverified or unparliamentary remarks whatsoever, that is defaming the plaintiff or any person related to the plaintiff with regard to the activities carried out in the School property;

Mandatory injunction directing defendant No.1 to publish an unconditional written apology for defendants No.2 to 4 to publish an unconditional apology in all their television channels for broadcasting the News item on and after 16.07.2018 which defamed the plaintiff and for costs of the suit and such other appropriate orders.

2. The brief averments of the plaint is as follows: -
Vidya Soudha Public School, under Sri Manjunatha Seva Trust, is a reputed co-educational institution in Bengaluru, affiliated with CISCE, enrolling approximately 778 students (Preparatory to Grade 10) and 550 pre-university students, known for high academic standards, quality education and adherence to Government safety norms.
2(a). The school is built on Plot No.6B, Peenya Industrial Area, acquired through the 1992 sale deed (8092 sq. mtrs.) by M/s.Vaishak Concrete Products, with 4102 sq.
mtrs. gifted to trustees in 2004.
The plaintiff obtained NOCs from BDA in 2013 and from KIADB in 2012, BBMP sanctioned Building Plans in 2014 and 2016 and Partial Occupancy Certificate in 2015.

Construction complies with the 1991 KIADB Act Amendment permitting educational institutions in industrial areas, supported by the judgments of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in 2012 and Hon'ble Supreme Court in 2015.
2(b). The defendant No.1 is a self-proclaimed RTI Activist known for filing frivolous cases to harass.

The defendants No.2 to 4 are Media Entities (Writemen Media's Public TV, Dighvijay 24X7 News) and Reporter - Maruthesh, accused of broadcasting unverified, sensationalized stories to boost viewership, disregarding their responsibility as media houses.
2(c).

From 16/17.07.2018, the defendants aired false reports alleging unauthorized school construction in a polluted industrial area, endangering ~1400 students,
violating KIADB/BBMP norms and falsely linking the plaintiff to politician H.D.Revanna.
These included TV programs, interviews, news tickers, video footage and website uploads as per Documents 9-13, ignoring plaintiff's clarifications and factual evidence.

2(e). The suit claims defamation per se.

The plaintiff seeks 1 Crore in damages,
permanent injunction to stop further defamatory broadcasts, mandatory apologies from defendants and litigation costs.

3. The brief averments of written statement filed by defendant No.1 is as follows:-
The suit is neither maintainable in law nor on facts and should be dismissed in limine.
This defendant denies the plaintiff's claim of being a reputed educational institution with high academic standards and world-class facilities, calling these claims false and demanding strict proof.
This defendant rejects assertions of safety norm compliance and quality education, requiring strict proof.

3(a). This defendant acknowledges the 1992 sale deed and 2004 gift deed, but contends that industrial land cannot be used for a school without legal authority,
alleging plaintiff suppressed this fact.
This defendant denies plaintiff's claim of valid NOCs from BDA and KIADB, asserting KIADB rejected jurisdiction and plaintiff misrepresented permissions.
This defendant denies compliance with KIADB, BDA and BBMP regulations, claiming unauthorized construction without proper approvals.

3(b). This defendant denies being a frivolous RTI Activist or filing cases to harass,
rejecting claims of concocting false stories.

The defendant No.1 denies malicious intent or defamation, asserting complaints to the Child Rights Commission were lawful to highlight plaintiff's violations in operating a school in a polluted industrial area.

3(c). This defendant rejects claims of sensationalizing or causing reputational harm,
asserting statements were true and based on legal complaints.
This defendant denies causing reputational damage, financial loss or blackmail, labeling plaintiff's allegations as concocted to cover up its violations.
This defendant rejects accusations of ignoring plaintiff's clarifications, claiming no clarifications were provided.
3(d). This defendant contends that plaintiff's reliance on court judgments on KIADB Act, Hon'ble High Court and Hon'ble Supreme Court rulings is irrelevant to the case.
3(e). This defendant denies the existence of valid cause of action, calling the suit speculative and baseless.
This defendant asserts plaintiff's claims of reputational harm and academic excellence are unproven and irrelevant.
This defendant requests for dismissal of the suit with exemplary costs.

4 4. The brief averments of written statement filed by defendant No.4 is as follows:-
The suit is frivolous, speculative and filed with malafide intent to suppress defendants' freedom of expression, liable to be dismissed in limine.
This defendant rejects plaintiff's claims of being a reputed Institution with high academic standards and quality facilities as self-serving and irrelevant, demanding strict proof.

4(a). This defendant acknowledges property acquisition documents 1992 sale deed,
2004 gift deed as matters of record, but deems allegations about NOCs and construction approvals partly irrelevant, requiring strict proof.
4(b). This defendant denies specific involvement in defamatory broadcasts or malicious intent, contending allegations are generalized, lack specificity and are partly false.
This defendant rejects claims of sensationalizing or damaging plaintiff's reputation, asserting plaintiff failed to provide clarifications.
This defendant denies linking plaintiff to H.D.Revanna or causing public chaos, calling such claims irresponsible and generalized.
4(c). This defendant rejects claims of causing reputational harm, financial loss or blackmail, asserting plaintiff's suit aims to cover up its own lapses and achieve oblique motives.
This defendant denies that plaintiff suffered humiliation or loss of public faith, contending allegations are unproven and lack necessary parties.
This defendant rejects plaintiff's arguments on press responsibility as irrelevant to this case.
4(d). This defendant denies that the plaintiff has a prima facie case or balance of convenience, asserting no cause of action exists and court fee is insufficient.
This defendant notes non-joinder of necessary parties i.e., Members of Society as a ground for dismissal.

This defendant on these grounds prays for dismissal of the suit with exemplary costs against defendant No.4.
5.

On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, my predecessor-in-office has framed the following issues for determination:-
ISSUES 1.
Whether plaintiff proves that defendants have defamed his reputation?
2. Whether plaintiff proves that he is entitled for sum of 1,00,00,000/- (Rupees one Crore Only) from defendants by way of compensation for defamation caused by them?
3. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the reliefs as sought?

sentences.text: 6. After settlement of issues, CAO of plaintiff Institution by name Sri.Mohan M. has entered into the witness box as PW.1 and Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 were marked through him and examined one witness by name Sri.Ramachadra Moger as PW.2.
The defendants No.1 and 4 neither adduced any oral evidence nor produced any documents.
7. Heard the arguments of plaintiff.
The defendants No.1 and 4 have not addressed their arguments.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1: In the affirmative.
 Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.4:

As per final order below  for the following:
 REASONS 9.

Issue No.1: - The plaintiff alleges defamation through false broadcasts by the defendants on July 16-17, 2018, claiming unauthorized construction on industrial land, endangering students and linking the plaintiff to politician H.D.Revanna.
The plaintiff asserts compliance with KIADB Act (1991 amendment), supported by BDA/ KIADB NOCs at Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.3, BBMP Building Plans as per Ex.P.4 and court rulings.
Plaintiff's evidence includes affidavit of PW-1, testimony of PW-2 and documents at Ex.P.5 to Ex.P.13, showing reputational harm due to unverified statements.
10. The defendant No.1 denies defamation, asserting his complaints to the Child Rights Commission were lawful to expose violations in operating a school in a polluted industrial area.
The defendant No.4 denies specific defamatory acts, calling allegations generalized and contending the suit suppresses free speech.
Both defendants demand strict proof and claim their actions were in public interest.

11. PW-1 confirm the plaintiff's compliance with legal requirements at Ex.P.2 to Ex.P.4, Ex.P.11 and Ex.P.12, supported by judicial decisions of Hon'ble Karnataka High Court in WA No.3135-3137/2010 and Hon'ble Supreme Court in SLP No.27778-816/2011.
12. Ex
. P.5 and
Ex . P.6

transcripts show that statement of defendants alleging unauthorized construction, student endangerment and political connections, which were not substantiated during trial due to absence of defendants.
13. The broadcasts at Ex.P.7, Ex.P.8, Ex.P.9 and Ex.P.10 were widely disseminated, potentially harming the reputation of plaintiff.
However, complaint of defendant No.1 to the Child Rights Commission suggests a public interest motive, though unverified claims amplified by defendants No.2 to 4 raise concerns of recklessness.

sentences.text: 6 14. "Subramanian Swamy v. Union of India, (2016) 7 SCC 221": Upholds criminal defamation as a reasonable restriction under Article 19(2), balancing freedom of speech (Article 19(1)(a)) with reputation (Article 21).

entities.text: Subramanian Swamy v. Union of India, (2016) 7 SCC 221
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Defamation requires intent or knowledge to harm reputation, which the plaintiff's evidence suggests through unverified broadcasts.
However, the court emphasizes that dissent and criticism are protected unless malicious or reckless.

15. "A.K.Subbaiah v. B.N.Garudachar, ILR 1987 KAR 100": Freedom of speech is not absolute;
defamatory statements require justification (truth or public good).
Defendants' failure to prove truth or public good weakens their defense, but their right to raise public concerns i.e., child safety must be weighed.
16. "Bijoyananda Patnaik v. Balakrushna Kar, AIR 1953 ORI 249":

entities.text: Bijoyananda Patnaik v. Balakrushna Kar, AIR 1953 ORI 249
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Press freedom does not permit unverified attacks on reputation, but public interest reporting is protected if done responsibly.
17. The defendants' right to free speech, including raising concerns about a school in an industrial area, is protected under Article 19(1)(a).

However, the broadcasts included unverified allegations i.e., pollution risks, political links that went beyond legitimate criticism, lacking evidence of public good under IPC Section 499, Exception 1.
18.

While the plaintiff's evidence establishes that the statements were false and potentially harmful,
the defendants' intent to highlight a public issue child safety in an industrial area aligns with free speech principles.
The absence of cross- examination limits assessment of their intent, but the reckless dissemination by media - defendants No.2 to 4 without verification suggests a degree of malice.
The plaintiff's reputation was likely harmed, but the defendants' freedom to raise public concerns must be protected unless clearly malicious.
19. The plaintiff proves that the statements were false and caused reputational harm, meeting the threshold for defamation per se under Section 499 of IPC.

However, considering the defendants'
freedom of expression and their public interest motive, the extent of malice is not fully established due to their absence and lack of evidence.
This Issue No.1 is decided in favour of the plaintiff, but since the defendants' actions may not have been entirely intentional, the remedies will be given with caution.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.

20. Issue No.2:- The plaintiff seeks 1 Crore for reputational harm, public suspicion, humiliation and reduced admissions, citing the defendants' wide viewership and failure to retract false statements.
21.
The defendant No.1 denies any loss, calling claims speculative.
The defendant No.4 rejects harm allegations, arguing the suit suppresses free speech.
22. PW-1 states reputational harm and reduced admissions, but no specific data i.e., admission records quantifies economic loss.
The defendants' wide viewership amplified harm, but the plaintiff's claim of 1 Crore is unsubstantiated by concrete evidence.

sentences.text: Awarding substantial damages risks chilling legitimate public interest reporting, as protected in the case of "Subramanian Swamy", which emphasizes balancing reputation with free speech.
The defendants' intent to raise child safety concerns, though poorly executed, aligns with public interest and heavy damages could deter such discourse.
24. "Rao Harnarain Singh Sheoji Singh v. AIR 1958 P&H 273": Damages are discretionary, adjusted based on harm gravity.

entities.text: Rao Harnarain Singh Sheoji Singh v. AIR 1958 P&H 273
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Here, lack of specific loss evidence suggests a lower quantum.
25. "A.K. Subbaiah Case": Defamatory statements without justification warrant damages, but the quantum must not unduly restrict free speech.
26. "Bottangada M. Raju v. Col. C.P.Muthanna": No Criteria to determine the quantum of damages and reduced the amount from 1 lakh to 75,000/-.

entities.text: Bottangada M. Raju v. Col. C.P.Muthanna
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 27. The plaintiff establishes reputational harm, actionable per se, but lacks evidence of specific economic loss.
To avoid suppressing defendants' freedom of speech, particularly their right to raise public concerns, a nominal compensation is appropriate.
5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lakhs) is deemed just, balancing the plaintiff's reputational harm with the defendants' right to free expression.
28. The plaintiff is entitled to 5,00,000/- as compensation, significantly reduced to protect defendants' freedom of speech.
Hence, Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
As per Issue No.2, 5,00,000/- is awarded instead of 1 Crore to avoid chilling free speech while addressing harm.
30. The plaintiff's evidence at Ex.P.5 to Ex.P.10 shows reckless broadcasts, but a broad injunction risks restricting legitimate reporting.

A limited injunction against repeating the specific false statements i.e., unauthorized construction, political links) is warranted, as per the case of "A.K.Subbaiah", to protect reputation without unduly curbing speech.
31. An apology is justified to mitigate harm, supported by the case of "Subramanian Swamy", but must be proportionate to avoid undue burden on defendants' expression rights.

32. The plaintiff is entitled to 5,00,000/- compensation, limited injunction, proportionate apology,
but not the full 1 Crore or unspecified reliefs.

Accordingly, Issue No.3 is answered partly in the The Management Vidya Soudha Public ... vs Narasimha Murthy T on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5202505/

sentences.text: 33. Issue No.4:
In view of the above discussions, this court proceed to pass the following:-

ORDER Suit of the plaintiff is partly decreed as follows:
The defendants, jointly and severally, shall pay 5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Only) to the plaintiff as compensation for defamation, reduced to protect the defendants' freedom of expression.

The order of permanent injunction is granted, restraining defendants No.1 to 4, their agents, representatives or anybody claiming through them from broadcasting or publishing the specific false statements made on July 16-17, 2018, regarding unauthorized construction, student endangerment or links to H.D.Revanna, through any media.

The order of mandatory injunction is issued, directing defendant No.1 to publish a written apology and defendants No.2 to 4 to broadcast a brief apology on their channels and websites within 60 days, acknowledging the unverified nature of the July 16-17, 2018 statements.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the parties to bear their own costs.
Draw decree accordingly.

ORDER Suit of the plaintiff is partly decreed as follows:
The defendants, jointly and severally, shall pay 5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Only) to the plaintiff as compensation for defamation, reduced to protect the defendants' freedom of expression.

The order of permanent injunction is granted, restraining defendants No.1 to 4, their agents, representatives or anybody claiming through them from broadcasting or publishing the specific false statements made on July 16-17, 2018, regarding unauthorized construction, student endangerment or links to H.D.Revanna, through any media.

The order of mandatory injunction is issued, directing defendant No.1 to publish a written apology and defendants No.2 to 4 to broadcast a brief apology on their channels and websites within 60 days, acknowledging the unverified nature of the July 16-17, 2018 statements.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the parties to bear their own costs.
